morning.title: Skyroot’s Raman-2 Engine Clears Acceptance Test for Vikram-1 Flight 2
morning.text:
Skyroot Aerospace has said that its Raman-2 has successfully cleared the acceptance test for Vikram-1’s Flight 2! Housed within the rocket’s Orbital Adjustment Module (OAM), Raman-2 plays a critical role in placing satellites into their intended orbits.
Fully 3D-printed and regeneratively cooled, the engine is designed for multiple restarts in space. Raman-II engine, which was designed by Skyroot to generate 820 N (Sea Level) and 1460 N (Vacuum) thrust, with a nominal chamber pressure of 8.5 bar absolute. The regeneratively cooled engine, manufactured through additive manufacturing techniques, utilizes Mono Methyl Hydrazine and Nitrogen Tetroxide as propellants.
Next up: integration with the OAM and electrical checks.

HAL Nashik Photograph Shows HTT-40 Assembly at 13th Aircraft Station
morning.text:
An image from the Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) Nashik Complex reveals more about the manufacture of the HTT-40 trainer. An illuminated board at the production line shows that the plane being produced is TH-4013, i.e. the thirteenth plane.
On November 19, 2026, the HAL Nashik Complex welcomed Shri APVS Prasad, Distinguished Scientist and Chief Executive (Airworthiness), Centre for Military Airworthiness and Certification (CEMILAC), and his team. During the visit, Combat Flight Test Bed (CFTB) was amongst the topics discussed.
The illuminated board at the production line shows the location as ‘HTT-40 Station – 13th A/C – TH-4013’. This indicates that the HAL Nashik Complex is currently manufacturing its thirteenth plane. Although the plane can be seen in the last stage of manufacture, this does not indicate that it has been manufactured, certified or supplied to the Indian Air Force.
Topics of discussion during the CEMILAC visit also included specification and speciality changes required for the CFTB. It was stated that CEMILAC will supply electronic airworthiness authorisations which should help to speed up the certification process. In addition to Prasad, senior personnel from HAL, CEMILAC and the Regional Centre for Military Airworthiness (RCMA) in Nashik were involved in the meeting.
This follows HAL’s drive to further utilise domestic planes and manufacturing resources for test purposes. The CFTB is designed to act as a specialised test asset. However, details of the exact specification of the CFTB as well as the particular changes that will be made to the HTT-40 were not given.
The HTT-40 is a trainer plane designed and manufactured indigenously by HAL. It is designed to fulfil the IAF’s need for training for the first stage of a pilot’s career. It includes a tandem seating layout, state-of-the-art electronic systems, air conditioning and zero-zero ejection seats. The plane is driven by a Honeywell TPE331-12B turboprop engine.
HAL has two HTT-40 manufacturing lines; one is based in Bengaluru and the other in Nashik. The latter was started in October 2025 and has therefore helped to further boost HAL’s HTT-40 production capability. The HAL Nashik Complex has specialised manufacturing sections for the production of the plane’s fuselage, wing and tail sections.
The Indian Air Force has placed an order for 70 HTT-40 planes at a cost of around ₹6,838 crore. HAL supplied the initial trio of HTT-40s to the IAF in September 2026 thereby commencing supply under this contract. The planes are anticipated to be used by the IAF to help train pilots in fundamental flying skills as it works to establish both an appropriate size force and training base.

morning.title: WSB Real Estate makes exits worth Rs 900 cr
morning.text: MUMBAI: Real estate-focused investment firm WSB Real Estate Partners has made exits worth Rs 960 crore from a total six mid-affordable housing projects against investments of around Rs 700 crore. The exits generated an average internal rate of return (IRR) of 19-21% and an investment multiple of 1.4 times.The six projects include developments by Wadhwa, Alliance, Sowparnika, Ultra Bright, Prateek Group and Vakratunda across Mumbai Metropolitan Region (MMR), Bengaluru and National Capital Region (NCR).The portfolio comprises three projects in Bengaluru, two in MMR and one in NCR. Bengaluru accounted for around 45% of the total investments, followed by MMR at 40% and NCR at 15%.WSB Real Estate Partners started investing in these projects in September 2022, with most investments made between October 2023 and November 2024. The average investment size was around Rs 100-125 crore, while the average holding period was around two-and-a-half to three years.“Our investment approach is based on evaluating opportunities supported by credible developers, strong project fundamentals and ongoing demand from the market. These exits reflect our ability to structure investments with appropriate safeguards and work closely with development partners to achieve successful repayments,” Jyoti Agarwal, Executive Director, WSB Real Estate Partners, told ET.According to her, most of these projects were exited prior to their originally envisaged tenure. The exits have been faster, which indicates that the projects have largely performed well in terms of sales and cash flows.The firm's investment strategy is focused on the mid-affordable housing segment, particularly projects in user-driven markets with established developers and strong execution track records.Most of the projects had secured necessary approvals and recorded initial sales when WSB invested, allowing cash flows to begin early in the investment cycle. Rising residential property prices across markets, particularly Bengaluru and Noida, also supported sales realisations and cash flows, helping accelerate capital recovery.The firm also benefited from investing in projects during the early stages of their development, after approvals were secured. Capital recovery was largely supported by project-level cash flows, while some investments were refinanced by other investors."Rising land prices have led developers to adopt joint development arrangements or move further away from established city centres. This has also led to the emergence of new micro-markets, particularly in Bengaluru," Agarwal said.Founded in 2013, WSB has committed around Rs 4,000 crore across more than 75 real estate investments. The firm is backed by the family offices of Allcargo Group, Navneet Education Limited, Mahavir Agency and BAsoil Advisory. Most of its existing funds are fully deployed, although the firm is evaluating co-investment opportunities and could consider launching another fund.Institutional investment in Indian real estate continues to reflect growing interest from both domestic and foreign investors, with capital flowing into multiple asset classes, including office, residential, warehousing and alternative real estate segments.Domestic investors are playing an increasingly important role in the market, while institutional capital is also supporting the development and expansion of organised real estate assets across the country.

morning.title: IIT Delhi Startup CYRAN AI Secures Investment From Singularity Fund
morning.text:
Singularity Strategic Autonomy Fund (SSAF) has invested in CYRAN AI Solutions , an IIT Delhi deep-tech company building sovereign enterprise and edge AI for defence and industry.
Defence, space, aerospace and precision manufacturing generate more sensor data than teams can review in time. Turning that data into fast decisions is now a strategic necessity, and for India it must run on sovereign technology. CYRAN fuses 20+ sensor types into a single operating picture, running offline at the edge or inside enterprise environments. It owns IP at every layer, from sensor fusion and AI pipelines to integrated systems.
→ Founder: Prof. Manan Suri, IIT Delhi faculty and head of its NVM & Neuromorphic Hardware Research Group. MIT Technology Review Innovator Under 35, with 20+ patents and 120+ publications.
→ Field-proven: One of 45 startups, out of 600+ in the iDEX ecosystem, to convert prototypes into procurement contracts, and now progressing under ADITI. In live deployments, data-to-insight time has dropped from days to minutes.
→ Validated technology & partnerships: An NVIDIA case study validated its gigapixel edge processing for in-orbit applications. Building low-power neuromorphic edge systems with Innatera (Netherlands), with prototypes for CES and SEMICON.
→ Industrial traction: Uses existing factory data to catch faults early and speed up inspection and clearance, from engines returning to service to satellites heading to launch. Signed a strategic MoU with Safran Aircraft Engines at Bharat Innovates 2026 in Nice, in the presence of PM Narendra Modi and President Emmanuel Macron.
CYRAN fits squarely within SSAF’s mandate: backing Indian-owned capability in the technologies that underpin national security and industrial competitiveness. We will work with the team to scale deployments, strengthen the offering and build an export path.
Thank you Prof. Suri & the entire CYRAN team for your trust. Proud to back a globally relevant sovereign AI stack for critical sectors.
EDITED BY RAUNAK KUNDE

morning.title: APL Apollo Tubes shares: Buy on dips or wait for a reversal after Monday's rout? Here's what charts suggest
morning.text: APL Apollo Tubes shares have remained under pressure since the announcement of its proposed deal with Tata Steel, plunging over 21% on Monday, November 23. The sell-off came even as Tata Steel acquired the first tranche of 2.77 crore shares from promoter entity S Gupta Holding Private Limited at Rs 2,100 apiece in a block deal worth around Rs 5,825 crore.Under the agreement, Tata Steel will acquire S Gupta Holding's entire 7.38 crore-share stake, representing 26.38% of APL Apollo's equity on a fully diluted basis, in three tranches. The deal also triggers an open offer to acquire up to 26% of the company's expanded voting share capital at Rs 2,301.40 per share.Investors are now faced with a dilemma: should they buy the dip in APL Apollo Tubes shares or wait for the stock to stabilise before taking fresh positions? From a technical perspective, analysts suggest waiting for a period of consolidation and signs of price stability before considering fresh accumulation.What do technical charts suggest?Osho Krishan, Chief Manager – Technical & Derivative Research at Angel One, said APL Apollo Tubes witnessed a sharp intraday correction of over 20% following developments surrounding its acquisition deal with Tata Steel, triggering significant selling pressure."From a technical perspective, the sharp decline has resulted in a breakdown of the prevailing price structure, negating the broader higher high–higher bottom formation and indicating a deterioration in the near-term technical outlook," he said.Krishan added that the stock appears vulnerable, with its price action likely to remain sensitive to further developments and clarity on acquisition-related news flow.On the downside, he flagged the Rs 1,580–1,600 zone as an important historical support area."The historical support zone of Rs 1,600–1,580 is expected to provide some cushion and could act as an important level to monitor. However, given the sharp breakdown and elevated volatility, investors should avoid aggressive dip buying," Krishan said.He added that investors should wait for a period of consolidation and signs of price stability before considering fresh accumulation.Where are the next support levels?Nagaraj Shetti, Senior Technical Research Analyst at HDFC Securities, also believes the stock's technical outlook has weakened following the sharp correction."After the deal, technically, the stock is looking sharply weak. Right now, the next near-term support is somewhere around Rs 1,505 to Rs 1,510, which is another Rs 40–45 lower," Shetti said.On the investment strategy, he advised investors to wait for greater clarity rather than rush to buy the stock on dips."I think it is better to wait for clarity. Unless and until the stock reverses sustainably, only then can we advise investors to accumulate at lower levels," he said.Shetti also pointed to around Rs 1,600 as an area where investors could look for accumulation.Disclosure: This article has been written by Kumar Gaurav, who is not a Sebi-registered Research Analyst or an Investment Adviser. morning.title: IAF Looks at a New Way to Keep Combat Aircraft Airborne for Longer
morning.text:
The Indian Air Force (IAF) is fiddling with the new concept of using Autonomous Unmanned Mid-Air Refuelers that could be used for refuelling jets that are part of the Compact Air Patrol (CAP) without risking larger manned mid-air refuelers close to the air defence coverage of the rival country.
IDRW has learned from its sources that while IAF is keen to focus on the procurement of manned mid-air refuelers like the Boeing MRTT based on the IAI-HAL technology of converting commercial Boeing jets into mid-air refuelers and even the procurement of next-gen mid-air refuelers like the Airbus A330 MRTT in the near future, it is closely monitoring some countries using drones as mid-air refuelers that can operate in contested airspace or closer to the borders so that the operations of the manned jets remain in the air for longer.
IDRW has been told of the advantages of using autonomous unmanned mid-air refuelers, that they will be much smaller in size and more attritable than manned mid-air refuelers that are juicy targets when being operated close to the border and are counted as force multipliers that are to be taken out in the event of war so that they can cripple the operations of the other side.
The emergence of long-range air defence systems will make it harder for mid-air refuelers to operate close to the border, and since these platforms are huge and have the largest radar cross section, they are also easier to track and target in the event of a conflict, due to which they need to have smaller autonomous unmanned mid-air refuelers that can carry 20000 kg of fuel, as seen in similar platforms.
Such a transfer of fuel on the Rafale or AMCA in the future could mean their combat radius could increase by 1852 kilometres; that could mean each Rafale could stay in the air for roughly 2 hours if standard fuel-efficient cruising speed is factored in. That is a great range for an aircraft that is on extended range of Compact Air Patrol (CAP).
IAF sources have not confirmed if it is looking inwards for such procurement, but it seems likely private sector companies can develop such medium-scale autonomous unmanned mid-air refuelers that, due to their low radar signature, will be a better option to use in airspace where threats of long-range air defence from across the border are real, and due to their smaller size, it will also mean they will not be easy to hit at extended range, which is not the case with manned mid-air refuelers.
RAUNAK KUNDE

morning.title: A ₹43,000 crore bet on banks and financial stocks: What changed in FIIs’ November flows?
morning.text: Foreign investors are back in Indian equities, but their November buying has come with a clear preference for banks and other financial stocks. FIIs poured ₹43,102 crore into the sector in the first 15 days of the month, more than half of total net buying of ₹84,292 crore across sectors.The scale of the shift stands out against the year’s broader trend. Financial services had been the biggest target of foreign selling, with net outflows of ₹81,217 crore so far in 2026. The November buying is the largest monthly inflow into the sector, yet it has not erased those year-to-date withdrawals.The buying is not confined to financials. Foreign investors also added ₹7,570 crore to telecom, ₹7,551 crore to autos and ₹6,519 crore to consumer services. IT drew ₹5,080 crore, while consumer staples saw ₹3,042 crore of net buying. Capital goods, by contrast, recorded the largest November outflow, at ₹3,781 crore, according to NSDL data.The turn towards financials comes after a strong Q2 earnings season. Jefferies said banks’ core profit, excluding treasury income, grew 23% year on year, above estimates, with higher net interest income and lower credit costs. Net interest income rose 13%, the fastest pace in 11 quarters, according to the brokerage’s review.HSBC also pointed to resilient credit growth and asset quality, while flagging margin compression at large private banks. Nomura’s analysis found that banks reported earnings ahead of consensus estimates in the quarter.Also Read |The great rotation begins! India’s MSCI EM weight jumps to 14.7% after two years of heavy FII sellingThe improvement extends beyond lenders. HSBC said Q2 earnings growth was the strongest since December 2023, with 67% of companies reporting results in line with or ahead of expectations. Excluding commodities, sales rose 17% and net income increased 19%. Jefferies reported 19% earnings growth for its coverage universe, excluding oil and gas and metals, and said earnings upgrades outnumbered downgrades for a second consecutive quarter.That backdrop may help explain why financials attracted the biggest share of the November flows. But the recovery is not uniform. HSBC noted that autos, staples and IT were relatively weaker in the quarter, while Jefferies flagged input cost pressure on margins in autos, staples and cement.As a result of the heavy FII buying, Nifty Bank is up over 14% this month and even hit a fresh all-time peak of 65,193 points.Nomura attributed the broader November surge in foreign buying to several factors: investors’ underweight positioning in India, lower crude and commodity prices, a stable rupee outlook, weakness in the AI trade, stronger earnings and expectations of a possible reduction in long-term capital gains tax.The flows have also coincided with a sharp rebound in Indian equities from their October lows. But the scale of the buying has not removed valuation concerns. Nomura said the Nifty’s one-year forward price-to-earnings multiple had recovered to 18.8 times. While that is within the 18–22 times range of the past four to five years, the index trades at a 65% premium to emerging markets, above its long-term average of 40%.Nomura cautioned that it expects the market’s advance to face “valuation resistance after the recent sharp move.”The November flows also suggest investors are returning selectively, rather than buying every sector. Telecom, autos and consumer services attracted sizeable investments, while capital goods remained a net selling category. Consumer staples, which saw foreign ownership decline for more than 12 quarters, received ₹3,042 crore in the first half of November. Jefferies said foreign investors had returned to Indian staples after more than a year of selling, though the sector remained underweight.(Data: Surbhi Khanna)(Disclaimer: Recommendations, suggestions, views and opinions given by the experts are their own. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

Kadet Defence’s JX3-30 Jet UAV Completes 50 Flights
morning.text:
Indian defence firm Kadet Defence Systems has celebrated the achievement of 50 sorties for its jet powered drone, the JX3-30. The company stated in an update on November 24 that the drone had flown at 5,000m and at speeds of 500km/h. It has also successfully completed strike and wave off exercises before being recovered successfully from Rajasthan’s Pokhran test site.
Furthermore, it has been used for operations on land and at sea. This demonstrates the increasing functionality of the drone and the development achieved through the completion of numerous sorties, said Kadet.
The JX3-30 (also known as Anudishya) is a jet powered drone which has been designed by Kadet Defence Systems to undertake a variety of defence related functions. It is predominantly utilised for simulating high speed aerial threats so personnel can train in the identification, monitoring and interception of these enhanced performance targets when compared to standard drone technology which is typically powered by a propeller.
In addition to this, the drone can be used for both decoy and testing purposes. As outlined in its literature, potential uses for the JX3-30 include air defence simulation, decoy packs, high speed target provision and kamikaze functionality. Adjustable attachments for the drone include radar enhancement devices, Luneberg lenses, infra-red flares, chaff and corner reflectors together with trailing targets.
According to previous technical information provided by the company, the drone is jet powered and has a flight time of in excess of one hour. Its maximum operating height is 8,000m and it can achieve speeds of around 150 metres per second. Although the maximum performance parameters for the drone are given in its literature, the recent update emphasises that it has been successfully flown at 500km/h and 5,000m.
For a drone which is used for training and testing, the achievement of 50 sorties is highly relevant. Furthermore, where a drone can be recovered then this may offer a more economical solution for companies wishing to undertake a number of training exercises when compared to those which are designed for one off use. Significantly, the latest update stresses the successful recovery of the drone having completed strike and wave off procedures.
Previously, Kadet has stated that the JX3-30 can be adapted for a range of purposes such as air defence simulation and decoy provision. By offering various attachable items, the drone is able to mimic specific radar and infra-red profiles. This allows defence forces to effectively test equipment such as radar and arms in a managed setting.

morning.title: GalaxEye Awards Bellatrix Aerospace Contract for Thrusters on 30 OptoSAR Satellites
morning.text:
Indian Space start up GalaxEye has selected Indian aerospace manufacturer Bellatrix Aerospace multi-year contract to supply in-space propulsion for 30 OptoSAR Gen-ll satellites. Company says this marks the largest B2B order between two Indian private space companies by satellite volume.
GalaxEye said the thrusters will become an integral part of our Archtop bus and it was announced at At IISC 2026.
“A constellation is not just 30 satellites. It is one system spread across the sky, and propulsion is what holds its shape.” –
Suyash Singh , Co-founder & CEO, GalaxEye.
It was Unveiled in the presence of Dr V. Narayanan, Secretary, Department of Space & Chairman, ISRO; Dr Pawan Goenka, Chairman, IN-SPACe; and AVM Manu Midha, Director General, Defence Space Agency.
Bellatrix’s Arka electric and Rudra green-propellant thrusters completed in-orbit qualification on ISRO’s PSLV-C58 POEM-3 platform in January 2024. Rudra also underwent an in-orbit firing on POEM-4 in January 2025.
GalaxEye combines synthetic aperture radar (SAR) with multispectral optical imaging on a single satellite. Its OptoSAR technology enables Earth observation through clouds, smoke and darkness.
Bellatrix will design, build, test and supply its Arka Hall-effect electric propulsion systems for GalaxEye’s planned 30-satellite constellation. The agreement represents a major domestic B2B procurement commitment between two Indian private space companies.
EDITED BY RAUNAK KUNDE

morning.title: Dell and HPE both say they’ve become ‘different companies’
morning.text:
Dell and HPE this week both told investors they’ve become “different companies.”

The two hardware giants made that assertion on their respective earnings calls this week. HPE went first, on Monday, when CEO Antonio Neri declared “We are now a fundamentally different company” after acquiring Juniper Networks and creating products “built to capitalize on the next phase of AI.”

On Tuesday, Dell’s chief operating officer and vice chairman Jeff Clarke declared “We are now a different company” because the Infrastructure Solutions Group (ISG) has become the source of “the vast majority of our profit and growth.”

HPE’s claim to having changed is perhaps more credible on the face of it, given that its acquisition of Juniper means it has become more of a networking player.

Dell hasn’t made significant additions to its hardware portfolio, but there’s a big difference in its sources of revenue, which three years ago was just about evenly split between its infrastructure and client devices. In its Tuesday announcement, Dell revealed ISG revenue grew 198 percent year over year to $42 billion, while CSG racked up three percent growth to $12.9 billion – meaning Dell is now predominantly an infrastructure company.

Clarke said he’s seen some companies deferring their PC purchases to buy AI hardware instead, and said Dell is re-assigning parts it ordered to build PCs and using them for servers instead.

Dell exited its Q3 with a backlog of $32 billion worth of AI servers and is clearly aware that investors might worry that’s not a useful metric because some buyers’ dreams of operating neoclouds have struck financial or regulatory barriers. Clarke assured investors that Dell is “highly selective about the partners we work with”

“Every AI order is vetted for access to capital, end customer quality, trade and export compliance, and access to land and power.”

HPE also has wrinkles in its AI business, because buyers won’t stand for fat margins and that’s dented the company’s profits a little. Neri was able to point to AI-related revenue also rising sharply, up 68.6 percent year over year to $11.3 billion, while overall revenue climbed 50 percent to reach $14.5 billion. Networking grew at a more relaxed 12 percent.

The CEO said HPE expects better growth ahead, because new server purchases create demand for networks and storage. He also pointed to HPE having the opportunity to sell its networking kit to other OEMs who build AMD’s Helios rack-scale systems. HPE predicted its next quarter will see revenue reach $14.0 billion to $14.6 billion, up 51 to 57 percent year over year.

Dell is also optimistic that AI buyers will spend on kit beyond servers and GPUs and updated its full-year revenue outlook to $202 billion, $10 billion above its previous forecasts and up 78 percent year over year. ®

morning.title: Half of NASA's aging Mars fleet knocked offline by technical issues
morning.text:
Two of NASA's four missions operating at Mars have suspended science operations after encountering separate technical issues in recent weeks.

The missions affected by the outages—hopefully temporary—are NASA's Perseverance rover and Odyssey orbiter. Both are operating beyond their original design lifetimes. Perseverance is in its sixth year exploring the surface of Mars, having collected rock and soil samples for eventual return to Earth. The rover is now studying the rim of a crater that once contained an ancient lake of liquid water. Odyssey arrived in orbit around Mars in 2001, and is the longest-lived Mars mission in history.

Losing its voice

The problem on Perseverance stems from the rover's communications system. The rover has two redundant UHF radios for high-rate communications with a fleet of orbiters that relay data to Earth. A separate X-band system is available for direct-to-Earth communications at a lower data rate.

morning.title: Microsoft's historic cloud outage exposed an engineering “fog of war”
morning.text:
According to internal memos reviewed by Reuters, Microsoft has declared a "Code Red" overhaul of its engineering response practices after the November 12 outage that lost access to Exchange Online, Teams, and Outlook for users worldwide.

Per the memos, Microsoft 365 Core President Jason Henderson described the outage as having the most customer impact in the history of Exchange Online. In a separate memo, Henderson wrote that an urgent production fix in a recent incident took five to six days to reach worldwide saturation. Microsoft's target for its most urgent security fixes is to move from detection to safe worldwide deployment in one hour. "Needless to say, we aren't here yet," Henderson wrote.

The memos, which Reuters reviewed but Microsoft has not published, outline the response to the November 12 disruption. The company's post-incident report, dated November 20, attributed the downtime to an undetected Windows scalability defect introduced in July, which caused lock contention in the gateway processes. A Teams traffic failover then dumped additional load onto infrastructure already under stress, as maintenance had left nearly 14 percent of gateway server capacity offline at the time of the incident.

morning.title: AI godfather Yann LeCun torches Anthropic CEO over AI gatekeeping
morning.text:
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei is taking heat from AI luminary Yann LeCun, one of the founding fathers of modern machine learning, because of the Claudefather's fear-mongering around open-weights models, which also happen to compete with his products.

In an X post this week, LeCun likened the Amodei's advocacy to a “new form of medieval obscurantism.”

“Dario’s spiel since GPT-2 has always been about hyping the dangers so that open models would be made illegal, and he would stay in control,” LeCun wrote in response to a now three-year-old video posted to the platform in which Amodei warned US Congress members about the dangers of open-weights models, the use of which could not be monitored or policed.

“He left OpenAI because he wasn’t going to have control. It’s like the Ottoman Empire banning the printing press for Arabic so they would keep in control of the dogma.”

LeCun is one of the most influential names in AI and ML. His team is credited with the development of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) in the late ’80s during his time at Bell Labs. He later oversaw the development of Meta’s Llama herd of models as chief AI scientist before shifting gears away from LLMs to world model architectures like JEPA. He has also been a strong proponent of open source AI development and open models.

Of the major model houses, Anthropic has taken the most hostile position against the adoption of open-weights models.

Despite advocating against the unregulated diffusion of open models for years, Anthropic’s fearmonger-in-chief has maintained that the company isn’t opposed to them. “Anthropic has never advocated for a ban on open-weights models,” Amodei wrote in a blog post earlier this year.

The executive has instead fomented fears over their potential misuse.

“Open-weights models — it does not matter whether they come from China or anywhere else — do potentially present a higher risk than closed models, because it is very difficult to apply guardrails to them or monitor their usage, and, once weights are released, they cannot be withdrawn,” the blog post read.

Amodei has repeatedly hammered these talking points over the past several years, including in the Senate hearing that solicited LeCun’s post.

Amodei has also called for measures, such as stricter export controls on the export of high-end accelerators to China; a crackdown on industrial-scale distillation operations, for which his company has previously accused Alibaba and other Chinese model devs; and mandating safety testing for sufficiently advanced open-weights models.

In other words, Anthropic doesn’t want all freely downloadable models banned, just the ones that Amodei thinks aren’t playing fair or are powerful enough to compete with its own.

LeCun isn’t the only one who has pushed back against anti-open-weights rhetoric in recent memory.

Earlier this summer, a cadre of tech titans, including Meta, Microsoft, IBM, Dell, and Nvidia, wrote an open letter [PDF] in support of open-weights models.

Open models “strengthen safety and cybersecurity, accelerate innovation and diffusion, and enable sovereignty,” Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said at the time. “The world needs both frontier closed models and frontier open models.”

As we previously reported, Nvidia’s future depends on its ability to sell to a diverse set of customers ranging from the big model houses like Anthropic and OpenAI to public clouds, neoclouds, and enterprises. And while many of these companies are perfectly happy to get their AI through Claude or ChatGPT, others, whether it be for regulatory or cost reasons, are not.

Earlier this month, we reported how British neobank Revolut cut their vibe coding tab by 10x by moving its roughly 2,000 employees from Claude to Z.AI’s GLM 5.1 running on a cluster of 56 Nvidia B200 GPUs.

The problem for Anthropic, and OpenAI for that matter, is the more enterprises that embrace open-weights models, the less likely they are to spring for Claude or ChatGPT.

The Register reached out to Anthropic for comment, but had not heard back at the time of publication. ®
